blocks.text: As stated above, the nominative case is the default, dictionary, singular form of a noun, and is used to denote the subject of a verb. As such, there are no rules for working out how to conjugate a singular word into this case, as it's already in it by default.

If you want to refer to a group of objects in the nominative, you use the plural, just like in English. Though there are no rules needed to form the nominative singular (just look the word up in the dictionary), there *are* rules for forming the plural. These are very simple to learn:

items: Masculine nouns add -ы to the end of the word, just like how we add 's' in English. For example, стол ('table') >> столы ('tables').

Feminine nouns that end in -а replace the vowel with -ы, while nouns that end in -я or -ь have -и. For example, машина ('car') >> машины ('cars'); свинья ('pig') >> свиньи ('pigs'); ночь ('night') >> ночи ('nights').
Neuter nouns that end in -о have -а in the nominative plural, while -е becomes -я: письмо ('letter') >> письма ('letters'); море ('sea') >> моря ('seas').

blocks.text: There is a spelling rule called the '7-letter spelling rule', so called because it comes into effect after seven letters: **к, г, х, ш, щ, ж**, and **ч**. When you remove the default ending from a word, you are left with the stem. If the stem ends in one of those seven letters, then you generally have to add an alternate ending. For example, **книга**, 'book', has the stem **книг-**, so it obeys the 7-letter rule. What to do when this spelling rule appears will be covered in each instance individually. However, the rule generally just requires the use of an 'alternate' noun ending.

For the nominative plural, if a masculine or feminine word ends in the 7-letter rule, you always use the ending **-и**, not **-ы**. So, although **книга**, 'book', ends in **-а**, its nominative plural is **книги**, as its stem ends in **г**.

exercises.why: **результат → результат** (nom. sg.). Masculine, inanimate, nominative singular in a hard consonant — declines like DLI's дом: N. дом. Ending — (no ending) → — (no ending).  **хороший → хороший** (nom. sg. m., agreeing with результат). Adjective type IV, sibilant (after ж, ч, ш, щ) — declines like DLI's хороший: N. хороший. Ending -ий → -ий.  Declension: sg. результат · результата · результату · результат · результатом · результате; pl. результаты · результатов · результатам · результаты · результатами · результатах.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).
